name: SEAGRAMMAR
description: Bacteria in the eelgrass (Zostera marina) rhizosphere meet a chemically diverse set of plant metabolites. SEAGRAMMAR tests whether they transform them according to biochemical rules keyed on recurring substructures, rules reusable enough to predict reactions on molecules that played no part in deriving them. This registration freezes, before any experimental data exist: (i) the rule-learning framework and its substructure vocabulary; (ii) the evaluation protocol, comprising three splits, the metrics, the rule admission gate of ≥2 distinct substrates and ≥5 distinct strains, and a pre-registered predictivity endpoint of within-compound strain ranking; (iii) three baselines, namely structure similarity, label frequency, and a model trained only on public terrestrial data; and (iv) the identities of six sealed hold-out compounds, which cannot change hereafter. Every metric in the deposited pilot is computed on simulated labels drawn by noisy-OR from the rule priors. It is a rule-recovery positive control, not a measurement, and carries no biological claim. Three substructure-vocabulary variants were run before this registration and all three are deposited in full.
